The service is quick and the food comes out fast, but you can see the rags they reuse to clean the tables and such. If I had seen that before, I would have not stayed. However, I was already eating so mind as well keep eating and hope for the best. Let me tell you, hot pot gives me back tummy always, but that night was beyond belief. I am not sure if it was due to all the oil in the spicy, but yet bland broth or I got ill, but it was not a good night. 

I was initially supposed to meet friends here for lunch, but they bailed. Boy am I happy they did. I don't think this will be a place I revisit again.
Great place to eat with friends. Quality and service were good. I did not try the hot pot so I can't speak to that but the kbbq was delicious

Probably a 2.5. Good vibes and the meat was good. The service was terrible. Legitimately one of the strangest experiences I've had at a restaurant. Waiters refused to give us some of the meat we ordered because it was hot pot meat... after putting it on our table. Throughout the meal waiters would come by and tend to our grill without saying a word or asking. One of these sessions lasted 5 minutes or longer. Several times the waiter tried to remove things and serve them to us despite us telling them we wanted to cook it longer and we could cook it ourselves.

Friday night, very busy, but they found us a spot for four. Great taste and bibimbaps were lovely and piping hot. Beef was also great on the grill - bigger rice bowls please (ate two and didn't touch the sides). Service pleasantly speedy, considering it was NY New Year time! A lot of folks having fun.

This place is a classic for ayce hotpot. It's so affordable and you get a free birthday meal if you come 3 days before or after your actual birthday with at least 3 other people! They also have super large tables that can seat ~10 people, which is a complete vibe since you won't have to split up your group into multiple tables.

I wouldn't say that the quality of the meat is super standout-ish: you get what you pay for. There's a ton of variety and I love the concept of having your own individual hot pot (no mystery meats/quail eggs disappearing forever). They have a sauce station downstairs and the most amazing fried buns and condensed milk right next to it.

Finally got a chance to try this place last night. reserved the table the day before. got to the table they only serve cold water no tea (unlike other hotpot places)  place the order via QR code. which is a hassle. 20 mins in, veggy got to the table first, (ask the waiter: he will check and lt us know) waited total of 50 mins to start eating. 
Shrimp paste is very bad (shrimp with flour paste) Mushy... 
there is no service at all..... 

never going back

I'm truly disappointed. This place has been my go-to for years a staple for celebrations like birthdays, graduation dinners, and countless other special occasions. Whenever there was something worth celebrating, this was always my first choice.

However, yesterday changed everything. My girlfriend and I planned to celebrate our anniversary and took great care to ensure everything was in order. Knowing it was a Friday night and that reservations aren't accepted for smaller parties, I called at 4:00 PM to ask if I should join the waitlist early. The person on the phone assured me it wouldn't be an issue, saying that two people could be seated anytime.

Still feeling uneasy, I called again at 5:00 PM before leaving to double-check. This time, I was told that no one was ahead of us in the waitlist queue, and that adding our names around 5:30 would be fine. Trusting her advice, I joined the waitlist right at 5:30. I received confirmation, and shortly after, another notification that someone else was ahead of us. A few minutes later, I received the final update that we were ready to be seated.

Yet, when we arrived at 6:15 as planned, we were told our seating time had been pushed back by THREE hours to prioritize larger groups. Let me be clear that I called TWICE after confirming the appointment and followed every instruction they gave me and yet somehow everything was ruined. The staff made it seem like accommodating a party of two on a Friday night was no big deal, but clearly, it was. Our plans for a special evening were ruined. We had to scramble to find another hot pot restaurant and completely readjust our evening.

What's worse is the false confidence they gave me both times I called, making me think there was absolutely no issue. If they had been honest with me, I could've adjusted or made alternate plans. Instead, they blatantly misled me. We had to scramble to find another hot pot restaurant at the last minute and completely salvage what was supposed to be a special evening.

This kind of treatment is outrageous. If you don't care about parties of two, just say so! Don't lead people on, ruin their nights, and then brush it off like it's no big deal. After years of supporting this place and bringing friends and family for special occasions, this is made me extremely disappointed?

While I've cherished the memories here over the years, this experience was unacceptable. Thank you for the good times in the past, but after last night, I won't be returning.

I came for a friend's birthday, which I highly recommend because that person's meal is free. We had 7 people at our party, but they put us in a 6-person table, which was okay except that one side of the people couldn't get a personal pot. There was a shared pot in the middle, but we opted out of it for more table space.

Here are some of my favorite parts of the experience:
I appreciate the variety they offer in terms of meats and vegetables. I especially appreciate the wintermelon and lotus root, which are a bit expensive when bought on their own.
- The service was also very fast as after we placed an order, the food came within 2 minutes.
- I appreciate that they came ever few minutes to check on our soup levels which I feel like other hot pot places are not as attentive about.
- The price was unbeatable. For $40 a person include tax and tip for dinner is pretty great.

Here are some things that I believe they can improve on:
- Not all the sauce bar bowls are clean. A lot of them still had a piece of rice or sauce drippings on them which was a bit gross.
- The meat is frozen over instead of freshly cut. Personally, I can't taste the difference in quality but I know that this may be a bit concerning for some.

Overall, not a bad place for AYCE hot pot, and will be back for more birthday celebrations in the future.

Staffs are friendly, came here on a cold day for hot pot. We were seated upstairs. They have all you can eat hot pot and bbq or you can do both! Approx $30 per person. The have the big pot to share or the individual pot. Birthday person can eat for free however, you will need a party of 4. You make your own sauce station in the back in the first level. 

Food: 4/5
Service: 4/5
Ambience: 4/5

We were a group of 5 people having barbecue Friday night.  We were expecting a nice Korean style barbecue...We were greatly disappointed.  After we made our selections,  food came out fast and complete....well,  that was where the good things ended.    First,  the electric grill was substantially under powered,  it was more like a slow cooker and it took a long time to grill the meat and as a result,  the barbecue favors of the meat were gone.  In addition,  the quality of the meat was really mediocre at best,   tasted like plastic with no meat favor,  I could hardly tell the difference between beef and pork...not to mention the steak tasted like rubber. The sauce station was dirty with about 1/3 of the sauces missing,  I guess the crew never bother to check and refill.   Oranges, fires, and soup trays were mostly empty for the entire evening.  The resturant was big,  and clean but the restrooms were dirty with water on the floor creating a slippery condiition.  
The receptionist standing in front of  front counter was really unprofessional and rude even by American standard,   and I think she must have hated her job....
Anyway,  there are plenty of choices around the area if you want to have hot pot and barbecue.
Love the all you can eat option. I always find myself stuffed after I go. The complimentary fried dough and condensed milk is also very yummy.
Love this place! really good options and fun environment. Its a big space so it never feels to crowded either

I been to 99 Favor in this location since it first open. it kept going down, down and down. very disappointed. the fatty beef and the lamb has the same taste, that's right...NO TASTE!
The service was great years ago. now, it's awful. no one come by. we keep having to wave the waiters down. They we too busy chit chatting among themselves. ridiculous!

Haven't tried much Hotpot in nyc honestly, but even from what I've had, this is a pretty poor option. The soupbase is alright, not that great tho. Meat quality seemed good but all i tried was beef and lamb. The compliments stop there...

The BBQ is barely even korean, so dont expect angthing close to kbbq. The sauce bar was very messy, and poorly stocked. The bathrooms were filthy. The service was poor, and not helpful when we asked questions. And there are no ventilation hoods over the tables, which i thought was standard practice at hotpot and bbq places. Overall this place does not feel well maintained, and kind of dilapidated and strange. 

I guess this place is popular mostly because its AYCE + location, but you can find something with way more bang for your buck .

$30 AYCE hotpot, what else could you ask for? The restaurant is incredibly efficient because they have QR codes per table so you don't need to wait on a waiter, you place the order yourself. They have great soup based, a self serve sauce station, they give you plenty of napkins/plates, and refill your water quickly. It is delicious and super well run!

I've been to a couple hotspot places in the city since moving here and this has to be my favorite one. The prices aren't bad (pretty typical for hot pot/kbbq). they have good options at the sauce bar and it is definitely a big restaurant so not really hard to get reservations or get a table last minute depending on the day. My only complaint is that the service can sometimes be lacking and it's pretty common for us to not get something that we've ordered and have to ask multiple times for it. But the staff is nice and we don't mind asking. all the vegetables are fresh and the meat fresh and tasty. One of my top spots in the city.
Hard pass on this. Not good imo but I'm not a fan of hotpot or Asian bbq generally. Affordable all you can eat though if you like that. I won't return
Great spot for a birthday had so much fun. Great vibes and food. Also they sang happy birthday

DO NOT EAT HERE. 

As someone who eats here on a regular basis and tells friends and people asking for a place to eat that they should go here I will NEVER recommend this place and actually tell people to stay away. I had some pretty bad service tonight so my table tipped based off of service. I always leave a tip even for poor service. So we left a tip and walked away and was flagged down while leaving asking if we forgot to leave more... when we started saying the service was poor they waved their hands at as basically encouraging us to leave.

The bathrooms are dirty, the service is poor (no cake cutting), I can't understand their English, and my command of Mandarin is much more advanced so not sure which they insist on using incomprehensible English. I will never come again after many years of coming here. The waitstaff stands there and does nothing. We experienced food poisoning.

99 Favor Taste is a popular AYCE hot pot and kbbq spot with multiple locations throughout NYC. For $29.99pp, you get a filling dinner where you'd probably spend even more elsewhere in the city. This location is spacious with high ceilings. When we arrived at 6pm on a weeknight, it was pretty empty, but filled up by the time we left. Once seated, there's a QR code to order all your meat and veggies. There's a huge variety and I like that there's photos in case you're not sure what something is.

I may have over-ordered in the first round, so that was enough for us. I enjoyed all the meat and seafood options. They offer a sauce bar for you to make your own sauces along with some mantou buns and fries. The hot items are pretty limited though, but their house sauce is delicious.

Overall, great AYCE hotpot spot --especially great for groups, but good for dates too. Everything was served quickly too.

The service is friendly and fast. We were able to make a rsvp for five people for Friday at 6 pm the day before so we would not have to wait. We were promptly seated at 6 pm and told we have two hours for ayce. We ordered for two hours and ate for 2.5 hours. They were very nice and accommodated one birthday dinner as well as did not charge for my 3 year old. 

There is a decent number of choices for ayce. They only have cabbage , AA veggies, spinach for leafy vegetables. The quality of the tofu skin was below average. The angus meat was quite good. The squid and fish were a pass. I was very happy they had fish roe balls. The fish balls were pretty good. I like that they had booths so my young one could run around behind us. The freebies like fries , fried mantou, orange and seaweed were a little sad looking. It is definitely a good value for around $30, but you get what you pay for. Not as luxurious as haidilao.
We got individual pots and the service was ok. It was such a fun vibe for group! We went for a birthday and they ate free. I'd come again.
A decent hotpot spot with affordable prices. The service is good, and they offer a wide variety of vegetables and meats to choose from.
This restaurant is the best one I have ever eaten in. It tastes good, is very hygienic, has a good environment and a very good service attitude.

This review is long overdue.  About nine of us ate there yesterday, but I've been there about 9 or 10 times.  
The food never disappoints and you always get your money's worth!  That's more than enough for me.  
If you've never been, worth giving them a chance.
Good hot pot spot. Would like to try the KBBQ here too another time. Lots of options for food. You can do an individual or shared pot.

Located in Chinatown, the restaurant was easy to find and had a modern look. The food was great- the typical hotpot spread. I tried the spicy broth and it was good but had a kick at the end. We went during lunch so it was a chill atmosphere, not too crowded. It was easy to order using the online website, allowing multiple people to order for the table. Price was good as well for AYCE!

Pretty big restaurant, nice atmosphere! The service was quick even though it's busy. We tried both hot pot and kbbq, everything we tried was yummy. I wish they had more options like bulgogi for kbbq but overall really good.

Do me a favor and check out 99 Favor Taste in Chinatown.  For $40 a person (at the time of writing), you can get AYCE hotpot AND BBQ?  What's great is the portions are big (doesn't matter since it's AYCE) and most things are fresh (shrimp is a little questionable).  You order from your phone after you scan the QR code on the table and the food just comes.  Within minutes of placing your order, the dishes magically appear!  It's a loud and smell environment though.  You WILL be coming out smelling like food so bring a plastic bag for your jacket (or not).  Also, lots of people celebrate their birthdays here apparently.  In the 2 hours we were here, I think they played the HBD song 6 times.  Oh, birthday person eats free.

I would be back one day but there's so much competition.  But for the price, 99 Favor Taste can't be beat.

99 Favor Taste is one of my favorite hot pot restaurants in the city. From the moment you walk into the restaurant, the staff is so kind and welcoming and explain how to place orders. I've been there twice, and the most recent time, I went with a group of five friends who have never been here before, and we all had an amazing time.

I find that the way their system runs is quite efficient too - you don't have to keep calling waiters over to order more food since you order everything online and everything is brought out to you quickly and efficiently. There's a QR code that each person scans, and everyone at the table orders in the same cart. The waiters then bring out the food you order to you quite quickly - I was really impressed with the speed that everything was prepared. 

The sauce station is amazing too - they have tons of options you can add to make your sauces for your food. This was probably one of the most fun parts, since we were sharing our different sauce recipes while making them. There are multiple sauce stations in the restaurants so there usually aren't long lines that you need to wait in, which is great.

My friends and I lovedddd the broths we got - I highly recommend the spicy individual for non-vegetarians! One of our friends is a vegetarian and 99 Favor Taste had tons of options for her to eat too, which is great because a many hotpot places don't have too many choices for people who don't eat meat. There is a vegetarian broth for vegetarians along with some of the more classic broths, but the variety overall was great. 

The cocktails and drinks are VERY well priced and looked delicious, the beer tasted cool and refreshing, and they have a 4 for $40 deal on soju, making it a fantastic place to unwind with friends on a Friday evening. Finally, the price for the hotpot itself was amazing - we each spent around $40 on food only for all of our side dishes. 

The waiters check up on you quite frequently, refilling your water and your broth, and the restaurant is clean and orderly and very well-decorated. The entire experience was efficient, enjoyable, and delicious. 99 Favor Taste has quickly become one of my favorite comfort restaurants and I will definitely be coming back! Also, a great time to visit is 3 days before, the day of, or 3 days after your birthday with a group of four people or more - you get to eat for free when they check your ID for your birthday! Such an amazing deal, highly recommend!
Great place to go if you can get enough friends for your birthday. Typical AYCE hot pot place.
Meat was a little chewy, but went in the middle of the day so it was slow and service was great.
Love the quality of food. Amazing BBQ experience. If you love BBQ this is the place to be!

Love this place
Had many options and great staff members
I will be coming back and do recommend this place

The worst hot pot place I had been! I never feel hungry when I left at all you can eat place, this is the first time! 
The fat beef taste horrible, I always can finish 2 order easily by myself, but this time our group can't even finish 3 order for everyone, because no one wants to eat.

They gave us the last room of the second floor, and most of the time no one serve us! We were party of 8, and half hot pot, half bbq, the bbq part no one serve and no one exchange the pan for us until we keep asking to change, we had been wait until it almost burn, can't even cook anymore than wait to ask the waiter to come to change for us.
Only one waiter serving in the second floor, and he couldn't able to finish cleaning then having his dinner, I'm not blaming on him, but the manager should give extra staffs while others on their meal break, and there still have customer eating.

While a lot of stuffs have to do it by myself to bring it on the table like take my own napkins, extra plates... or clean the dishes on the table.... 
This place I will say it not clean at all! I will NEVER come again! If not getting a free birthday meal, and the Brooklyn 99 was under construction, I will never come to Chinatown 99.

P.S.: after I had a dinner in Chinatown 99, I found out I was positive of COVID few days after, and I didn't usually go out because I got pregnant. That was a very bad time for me and my family having a dinner in 99chinatown.

Around dinner time, the place becomes pretty busy. However, the restaurant is pretty spacious and I didn't feel bothered by the steam and smoke arising from the various hot pots and BBQ grills. 

My family got both hot pot and BBQ when we were there, but I don't think it was worth it. There were a lot of options and limited space in our stomachs. What ended up happening was we ordered some BBQ and mostly hot pot ingredients for everything else. Also, it's kind of a multi-tasking experience since now the restaurant has you cook your own BBQ as well. So, while you're minding your hot pot, you'll also have to watch the grill. 

I still enjoy making my own sauce concoction whenever I come. 

Overall, would not mind coming again.

Went for my friend's birthday on a whim! We grabbed an early dinner right after work, which was a good idea because the place was packed really fast! There were also tons of other birthdays in the house, since birthday people eat for free. We did hot pot and it was fun and great. They had a wide variety of vegatable and fish options, which was perfect because I don't eat meat and sometimes hot pot is very meat oriented. The broth was flavorful, the ingredients super fresh, and I loved the sauce bar on the side. Made a great soy/hoisin/sesame past mixture that went great with my hot pot. Lively ambiance and the interior is really clean and has an open concept so there can be lots of people but it doesn't feel crowded. I'd for sure come again.

Came here to celebrate a birthday with a group of friends. This is a must try location for birthdays. Staff played a song and gave a scoop of ice cream with a lit candle. If it's your birthday you eat for free. Everything came out to about $40 per person for AYCE hot pot. Making a reservation was quick and easy. Just a phone call and a quick confirmation. I was able to get a table for 10 people. We were huddled into our own private booth. Ordering food was easy. Just had to scan a QR code on our table and add what we wanted to the cart. Everything tasted good and we got our money's worth. I already plan on going again next year and I'm sure my friends may do the same on their birthdays. Most of them never had hot pot and walked away enjoying the nice surprise. I cannot recommend this place enough and look forward to coming back.

Cheapest AYCE hot pot there is! $30 pretax becomes under $40 after tax, cash discount, and tip. Maybe slightly less options on things like thick vermicelli noodles, but they have more than one kind of beef which I appreciate at this price point since other places will be more expensive and have one kind of beef - all my homies love 99 Favor

Great place for a get together

Pro
- fairly priced for NY standard. 30$ hotpot AYCE with kbbq as an option but we didn't do kbbq
- service is good
- easy to order on mobile
- lots of good dip
- seated pretty fast during dinner time on a Friday night 

Con
- can't really think of any for the price you pay. Nothing stood out as terrible

This place definitely gets super busy and there are nights you have to make a reservation just to get a seat or there is an hour or two wait. But you can also get lucky and there are some days not as busy and you can just walk in. I do recommend to try to go during the day and not at night because you're kind of being rushed out. Also at night the sauce stand where you mix the sauces is completely empty and filthy sauce and toppings smeared all over the place and it's honestly just gross. I am still giving them a 3 star rating because the food is good everything comes quickly and it's a fun experience especially with friends!

I don't like the food here. It's not very good, but the birthday special has me coming here some years. I don't believe it is ever worth it if theres a wait, but if you're left with no other options for hotpot or chinese BBQ, this will suffice.

My partner and I went to 99 Favor Taste for the birthday meal since their deal  is that birthday person eats free! I've been to the 99 in Flushing (which I think is closed now) so I went into it with okay expectations and they were met. The service was nice, the ambiance was nice, but the air was thick and the floors/tables were a bit oily and dirty. The sauce bar was small and a bit lacking. The food options were just okay. I'm not sure I'm inclined to come back if it wasn't for the birthday deal!

my family and i were in new york on vacation and wanted to stop in at 99 Favor Taste for dinner. we had lots of recommendations and saw positive reviews. there was quick service since we order everything ourselves. hotpot was delicious, but i would skip the kbbq if i were to ever come back. everything was great until it came to checking out.. no one came to give us a check, so after 35 mins we had to go up to the front. we payed and then as soon as we walk out the door we are yelled by a rude employee to leave MORE TIP! we left 15% which was more than enough since we ordered our own items, were served canned drinks and had to run down to get a check. i will never come back to this place even though the food was great. s

Service was bad. Our server put the food to grill and left ... and never came back. Everything was ruined and she explained they were only 2 on the floor.
Maybe, but some locals got perfect service while we waisted an hour.
We finally decided to leave. At least they offered us to only pay for 1 client, not 2, although it was worth it zero.

Great place to have your birthday because it's free within a few days of your birthday. It's also quite large inside so you can have a big party in one of the booths - like it was very easy to fit 6 people. You can pick bbq, hotpot, or both - and the table can pick different things. Service is fast and all the food comes quickly. Ordering is done on your phone so you can add things very easily.

Sauce bar is average, but nothing special. They have all of the usual suspects and the Chinese seaweed salad thing. It looked like some spots were missing dishes though, so maybe they have more dishes usually. 

The selection for the bbq meats is good and extensive. The thinner brisket ones were definitely fattier, but there were some other cuts of meat that were so good. Definitely just order a bunch and try everything. Meats were well seasoned and went well with the sauce bar. Hotpot also had an extensive selection of fish balls, seaweed, meats, quail eggs, all kinds of tofu, and vegetables. Their youtiao was not fresh though.

So I went to the branch in Chinatown at lunchtime on a weekday,  the place was almost empty,  we got seated right away... they give you the option of hot pot,  bbq, or both.  And if  1 person gets hot pot and the other bbq, you can't share. It's all you can eat. 
I ordered the spicy veggie broth,  and man,  that was no joke!  It was extremely spicy.... and for me to say that,  it's something!  It was so spicy that I actually had to use my sauces to cool it down... it was not enjoyable.  
You go online and select what you want to add to your broth. So there's limited interaction with the staff.  I was vegan at the time,  so I can't comment on the meats,  but they looked and smelled really good.  As for the veggies,  they are a bit more limited than the open buffets I've been to... but there's more than enough to stuff yourself.  When you request the greens, they give you a basket of about 5 greens (spinach, dandelion, bok choy, cabbage,  and others).  The sauce making  station was alright... they didn't have fish sauce or fresh chili...
I think that I have to go again and try the bbq before I give it a final judgment,  and maybe I should try one of the meat broths... but I don't know...

A great hot pot restaurant if you want AYCE. They had a good amount of options to choose from. Super spaciois restaurant with two floors and many seats for groups of people. Came here to celebrate a friend's birthday and they have sectioned-off rooms for large parties which makes it more intimate and super fun.

99 Favor Taste, where you can cook Chinese hot pot or Korean BBQ at your own table, was a great spot for dinner with a group of friends.  It was engaging, tasty, and fun.  One of my friends had to call to make a reservation, as doing so was not available online.  I was worried that she would have a hard time securing one, but the space was rather large and not super crowded.  We were seated in a booth where the cooktop table was made for whatever kind of meal you wanted to enjoy.  So, while there were stove ranges for hot pot, we had all decided to do only Korean BBQ and utilize the electric grill.  Our first grill wound up not working, and after about 30 wasted minutes trying to cook some beef, the staff noticed and replaced our grill.

The menu was available on your phone through a QR code, which was also tied to your table.  So, we placed our order, and the servers knew exactly where to deliver it.  The restaurant offered a flat fee for all-you-could-eat BBQ, but I was annoyed to discover that this fee only included meats, seafood, and bowls of white rice; everything else had a separate cost.  They provided no banchan or starters/sides with the meal.  There was, however, a buffet of sauces for your meats.  We ordered a variety of beef, pork, chicken, and shellfish proteins, as well as mushrooms and jalapenos.  A lot of the meats looked very fatty, so I stuck to the leaner ones, which I still found chewy.  Everything was well-marinated and flavorful, but the quality of the meat or the cuts were suspect.  Of everything we tried, my favorites were the shrimp, which were garlicky and plump, and the zesty black pepper steak.  The curry chicken was tasty, but the texture was slimy.   

Overall, I thought the food was fine, and it was a good deal pricewise.  However, I had definitely had better Korean BBQ elsewhere.

Great all you can eat hotpot. Can get messy but thats somewhat expected. Service isn't always the most attentive, but so long as your ordering is well timed and spread out it, there shouldn't be an issue with waiting too long for food. Sauce bar is extensive, and usually always stocked. The vibe can get a bit loud, especially with all the birthdays (lol), but its about the same as any all you can eat place like this.

The Korean bbq here is not very good but I enjoy their hot pot. The meat is standard but their price is better than competitors like hometown hot pot and bbq. We had a weird experience where the lights went out and my sister found a bug in her broth but this was years ago. The hot pot is probably a 4 but the bbq was a 3 so I would like to give it a 3.5 but alas

Truly a great group experience in NY with a variety of flavorful options in a lively environment. 

Setting: Very busy, but spacious restaurant. Do expect a longer wait if you don't have a reservation. Although my party had a reservation we faced a wait time which was disappointing. 

Service: Since the restaurant is packed, service was on the slower side which was unfortunate given the time limit. Nonetheless, the staff was kind! 

Food: Truly the highlight! With many options between hot pot and/or KBBQ, the sauce bar is a great addition as well.

Service is super quick, ambiance is fine but the birthday song goes off too often. Amazing selection of meats and veggies- pretty good bang for your buck. Sauce bar is decent too but don't expect much out of the sesame sauce- tastes like watered down peanut butter. The broths are also decent but it's not top notch like a more focused expensive hot pot place might be. Still good though and overall well worth your money for $30 ayce, considering that eating a mid dinner at a trendy restaurant in Manhattan costs like $50. This place is above mid. And I have socal / Bay Area standards for hot pot k? 

The lotus root is poppin. Thick cut and stringy, like fresh. Wood ear mushrooms are a lil dry.

We tried the hotpot and bbq unlimited special and really enjoyed it. I loved that you can just keep adding on the app and it'll start coming in without waiting to ask a waiter. The sauce bar was a little small but had some great options. For the meats and veggies there were all sorts of options you can think of and definitely worth trying something new! For two ppl unlimited hotpot and bbq plus two Sapporos we paid $97.97 before tip.

All you can eat bbq & hot pot buffet. Make your own condiments bar. Service is attentive, 1 item order through app came later than the others. Birthday boy ate for free 3 days before his birthday and three days after he changed residency. Good for our group bonding. They have a larger private seating room upstairs for 10+ people. They take reservations.
Amazing deal and fun experience.  The restaurant run its business like clockwork.  Kids eat for 50% off, and birthday dinners are free with ID.
Terrible service, the reception just standing there looking down at the table, took 10min to realize there are people waiting to be seated. Food is fine for the price.

Out of all the hot pot places in the city, 99 Favor Taste is the one that I keep coming back to. I've honestly been here too many times to count. I last came on a Friday night and was able to get a table immediately. Even if there is a wait for tables, I've never had to wait for long.

What I love most about 99 Favor Taste is that it's AYCE at an affordable price. They have a wide selection to choose from, and everything is surprisingly good quality, including the seafood. I think the broths are pretty flavorful, and their sauce bar is huge too. Depending on where you sit, you either get the big pot with the dividers or you get an individual pot. I will say that the service is not the greatest. They're not always the friendliest or most helpful, but it's always busy there at night, so I can see why.

If you go here for your birthday, your meal is free. I know people who hate how often they play the Happy Birthday song, but I think it's just part of the charm of the place. I'm giving this place 4 stars because it just can't compete with all the fancy a la carte hot pot places in terms of the ingredients and quality, but I'll definitely keep coming back here when I just wanna stuff my face.

I came in with a group of 12 for my birthday with a res and they were able to fit us all in a room, which was really nice. I like that you use your phone to order because taking orders from 12 people would have been so hectic, but it took a long time for us to get our food and we never got everything we would order. Granted we ordered a lot of food because there were so many of us, but we had to keep spamming our orders so that we would get them. The servers were kind enough to let us stay past the 2 hours, even though they kept saying that we only had two hours from the time of our res at the beginning,  because we were a little late. They played the birthday song for me through the speakers in the room which was really fun. They had a huge variety of food to choose from which was great and the quality of the meats was pretty good as well. I got the tomato broth and it was really flavorful. I would definitely come again!

Best bang for your buck KBBQ in NYC. great that there is hotpot too which makes for a nice sauce bar that allows you to dip your bbq meat in your own concoction. Only issue I had was that sometimes the service was a little slow so the meat wasn't cooked properly here and there. The ambiance is great and the place has a great deal for your birthday (free meal).

still a solid hotpot .. note everything is ordered via App now and the reception stinks so you will definitely use their wifi .. 5% savings if you use cash .. also they charge Tax .. when the birthday song comes on the restaurant speakers, it is way too loud.

We were a group of 13 who went for dinner on Sunday evening, the place was packed and rockin'. In fact the din was almost unbearable. Every. 5 minutes the noise level increased even more when someone's birthday was announced. In fact,  the whole experience was confusing. Ordering from the online menu was complicated for 13 people and we were in a very small room open on one side to the din where there was no ventilation. While most people had a small individual hotpot heated by an induction plate which was difficult to operate, four of our party elected to have their hotpot in a more "traditional" manner -- on an open gas burner. Stupid. One elder diner actually fainted from oxygen deprivation. So there's all that. And the food? It was delicious. Everyone order whatever they wanted and ate themselves to death. Total cost? $39/per person and our birthday girl ate free.

I'm confused as to what the name of this restaurant means, but nonetheless I had a great experience with the hotpot here! Truly a solid value in NYC's Chinatown for all you can eat, and it's open pretty late too! We each got the hotpot and tried the soju special-- 4 bottles for $40. We had a enjoyed a long meal here and didn't feel rushed at all.

Yeah my friends got hot pot and BBQ but. I got BBQ and the grill didn't get that hot and had to wait a long time for meat to cook, definitely not worth it they came out with small portions of meat and the workers didn't come around that often

I would give this place 0 stars if I could. It took 15-20 mins to get raw food we have to cook from the kitchen to our table, which did not make sense seeing that the place was half empty. We ordered a large amount of crabs, squid, beef, mushrooms and mussels for my table of 5 as we are starving. They brought of a 5oz portion of the 4 out of 5 foods mentioned above for us and did not disclose the fact that some of the food we ordered was out of stock leaving us to wait 20-30 for our food. We tried stopping the staff many times but they would just walk away. We had to track down a server and after he talked to us about the problem he also disappeared. And one more thing make sure the table you get is working! Half of the stove on our table is not working properly, or just not functional. The bbq grill is also not working properly! The right half is working and the left half of the grill is not. We place food on the grill and it took a long time to cook and when we asked to switch table they insisted that all the tables are the same. They tried to charge us 2 people that came at the end of time limit and they did not eat anything. They did not take off the drink we sent back from the check. The place is flushing is better but they are temporarily closed. We will not be coming back here and thank you for the worst buffet lunch experience in my life.

I definitely see the appeal of this place. You can fill up to your heart's content with a surprisingly expansive menu of AYCE hot pot offerings. The price is pretty good value by NYC standards. The free sauce bar is also very well-stocked.

My main gripe though was that the soup broth was really bland, so I found myself dousing my food with sauce to make it actually taste like something. While not egregiously so, the place also felt a tad grimy, which is somewhat to be expected at this price point, but it certainly didn't help my appetite. 

The crowd here seemed to be pretty young- seemingly college-aged or just a few years out. Maybe I'm just getting old and the thought of stuffing my face with average AYCE hot pot isn't as appealing as it used to be in the day. Not bad, but I wouldn't come back given all the great options for hot pot in the city.

We celebrated a friend's birthday at 99 Favor Taste (birthdays eat free!) with all you can eat hotpot. We were a party of 7 (made a reservation) and could all sit comfortably at the table. 

I would recommend bringing cash (5% off) and eating with a birthday to save a bit more. We had one birthday in the party of seven and ended up spending about $33 per person. 

You order on your phone, and it's cool because the whole table can submit and add items that they want. The service was also very fast. Our table also came with the option of individual pots and shared pots, so people were able to get different broths. 

I thought the selection of meats, vegetables, seafoods, and other items were really expansive and great for hotpot. i really enjoyed the shrimp
paste (which is usually a specialty item) and fried tofu skin in particular. Unfortunately, the broth (original and spicy) were not too flavorful, so you do have to rely on their sauce bar, which is included in the AYCE. 

I thought the hotpot stoves were a bit weak, so it would take a bit longer for things to reach a boil compared to other places I've been. 

Overall, this meal felt like a great value. I would definitely come back again in a group setting!

A friend that lives in the area recommended this place & I thought it was really good! It was honestly really cheap for New York. I was researching other hotpot places & I rarely saw anything that was all you can eat. You order on your phone & add it to the cart & the servers bring out the plates. Everything came out quickly & the food wasn't bad quality either. There was a wait because we came on a weekend at night but the wait was only like 15 minutes. I feel like this place is definitely worth it & probably the best option for all you can eat. Another plus is that you can do both kbbq & hotpot! Great spot to come with friends & perfect choice during the cold weather too.
The food was okay. They had a very good selection at the sauce station. They had a decent selection of meats and seafood but not as many as expected. Not bad for all you can eat grill and hotpot.

SCAM- SHADY BUSINESS PRACTICES. went in for a birthday meal and they said the standard 18 percent tip on 32 bill is 11 bucks. becareful everyone. They were also slow serving us bc we said birthday meal.

Good bang for your buck type of hot pot experience. We sat down and got a table with individual hot pots at our seats which was good, but not all of the pots were working right away. Overall, I'd say this is the value play hot pot experience but service could be better and they also don't bring out all the food that you order on the app so you have to flag down service to try and bring it to you.
Overall a great experience. A bit confusing at first with how the flow of things were to work, but a great deal for what it is. Lots of choices and excellent sauce bar.

tl/dr; for the accustomed, another wonderful lunch. Don't expect 'training wheels' here (e.g., extra help, explanations, communication). 

Had a very nice meal with friends who have never been.  She explained the experience as 'frenetic' - fast and energetic in a rather wild and uncontrolled way. 

I think this summed up 99 Favor yesterday. The mobile site to order wasn't working for broth. We couldn't get the broths ordered properly, and when you're hungry and waiting for broth, unsure if it's ever coming out or not, is not a good thing. To make it worse, our hotpot food items came out before the broths did. Some things were never brought out (like lettuce), and we were never checked on. We had to make a distressed call for help for things like more water to drink or when our pots were dangerously low. For BBQ, my newbie friend did marinaded meats first and got the grill all gunked up. Thankfully, service knew we wanted it changed when we turned it off, cleared it, and ordered more meats. 

Some of the items were not my favorite, like the premium pork. We didn't get too adventurous yesterday, I would have liked some items. 

But I never saw any of these things as an issue. I've come to accept this as the way of life with 99 Favor - suppose it took a newbie for me to realize just how chaotic it all can be.  And all the proteins and vegetables were all otherwise really good!  We had a very nice time and enjoyed a leisurely self-paced afternoon.

I've been to this location three times. I think there used to be one on Bowery or Elizabeth street? And I used to go there when I was in high school. This one is on the opposite side of the D train and I think it's bigger. Every time I've been, it has been with quite a large party and we always got seated in one of the "private" rooms upstairs. 

I made a reservation for ten people and because we are incapable of getting it together we were all pretty much 15 minutes late. They still seated us and even let us have the whole two hours from the time they sat us and not from the reservation time. Much appreciated! They're very nice!

I highly recommend the fish balls that have the fish roe in them. Those are my favorite here and I usually don't see them at other hotpot places.

Came here for all you can eat BBQ.  The place is nice and roomy.  Once we sat down,  you will need to scan QR code for the menu to place order.  Drinks menu is complicated, trying to get hot sake and don't see it.  Got cold one instead, cold don't taste as good as hot one.  We try to order some appetizers, but it cost extra $$, even seafood pancake cost $2.99.  Wow.. All the beef that we ordered, they were low quality of beef.  Every type of beef we cooked, they were cook medium, and they were still very chewy.  Service is ok.  This place used to be pretty good, don't know what happen.  Would not go back again.

My daughter moved to NY which I am kind of worry, but everything end up very good for her! She get to visit so many different kind of Chinese restaurants, I am so excited she 
All you can eat BBQ under $40 per person. I had a good time there.

After a super long time of walking past this place and seeing it packed every time, we finally were able to stop by. We put our names down on the waitlist around 6pm on a Saturday night, were quoted 1.5h, and weren't seated until about 7:45pm. So, prepare yourself for a long wait! 

Once you get in, the ordering is all via QR code at your table, which is super convenient. The dishes all come very fast too! That being said, I think it depends on the physical table you're seated at whether you get small individual pots or one big pot with partitions for different broths. The two of us were seated somewhere with individual pots which was a bit of a bummer as it was inconvenient to share both (and on the menu, they even have a big pot option with three sections - a huge pro over most other hot pot places that we didn't get to try!). I'm sure we could've requested another table, but given how long our wait already was, we didn't. 

The restaurant seems like a pretty popular place with people trying hot pot for the first time - they make the experience accessible, but this can also slow things down a bit when it comes to being able to flag someone down or get to the sauce station if you know what you want. 

Overall, this is a solid hot pot spot, and it's great they're open so late! It seems like they have an awesome birthday deal as well - as many people have mentioned, you'll probably hear multiple instances of the birthday song played as you dine. That being said, this probably won't be one of my go-to spots due to those small inconveniences and the abundance of other spots not too far away, but I'm sure I'll be back at some point.

Finally came here after many years of hearing about it. I was well aware that this is a go to place to celebrate someone's birthday. I decided to come here and celebrate my friends' birthday. It was very nice for all you can eat and it includes meats, something I didn't see in other hot pot places. I like that you can do both Korean barbecue and hot pot here. For a large group of seven people there was only one barbecue grill and since I don't eat non halal meat, I decided to only go for the hot pot option.  I feel like everything I'm saying is probably going to be mentioned in other reviews but here's some things that I wanted to point out that I hope would be helpful for other people.

1) It is all you can eat, so be prepared to come here hungry. Any unfinished food is charged by the pound. 
Fortunately, there were a lot of people in our group who had a good appetite! Lol
2) you can conveniently order through the QR code, and add items. The QR code is connected to everyone in that table, so they will be able to see what's being added through their phones too, and can keep track of not over ordering
3) If you eat exactly on your birthday, I believe you do not need a cake. We still got a cake though because we really wanted it.

Overall, I really enjoyed my time here. Would definitely come again !

My family came here to celebrate my dad's birthday and it was the perfect spot! If it's the day of your birthday, they get their meal for free. It was super easy to order by scanning their QR code. After ordering, the items came out pretty quick. They also have a station where you could build your own sauce!

Great authentic spot for authentic Chinese hotpot and Korean bbq. We came here with a large group and we're attentively taken care of. What's great is you eat free on your birthday so it's the perfect spot to bring a group. They also have desserts like cheesecake and ice cream. I loved the variety of dishes they offered and also there was a mascot singing you happy birthday. Super fun spot! Would highly recommend.

Came here on a friday night in a big group (~9). We made a reservation the same day, but 8 PM was the only time available. We were able to sit down before our entire group was here which was very nice.

The restaurant is very large for downtown Manhattan, with booths that can seat 4 on each side. The large booths have induction cookers for both individual small hot pots or a communal large hot pot. It also has one smallish grill. You order most things on the phone using a QR code posted at the booth. If you come in a large group, only ~4 people will be able to reach the hot pot, and the other 4 will reach the grill. 

There was a pretty large selection for both hot pot and kbbq, definitely more for hot pot but that also includes vegetables and other hot pot specific things. Unlike most of the other hot pot places I've been to in NYC, 99 Flavor Taste allows you to order as many dishes as you want at any time. This prevents waiting on the server to bring you more food and you can have bites of several different things at once, but makes it a lot more likely for you to overorder. 

Another thing: if you come here on your birthday then its free! They also sing happy birthday to you too, we heard it several times during our dinner.

One of the first hot pot places I tried and thought it was more low key compared to other places. Not as big and didn't feel like a ton of options but still one to keep in mind if other places have way too long of a wait plus there are multiple locations. 

There were lots of birthdays during our dinner so many songs were sang - probably at least 3-4 while we were there. I wouldn't recommend a big group here - we were just a party of 2 but I can't imagine doing more than 5-6 people.

Service was not that frequent - it's a lot of just trying to gather your dishes and flip the table as quickly as possible. I'd come here again if I needed a hot pot spot asap but not a top pick.

RATING: 7.3/10 

PRO TIP: If you're looking for authentic and tried and true hot pot, this is it. I grew up eating here often in high school so this chain holds nostalgia. 

DO: order multiple soup bases, try the fuzhounese fish balls (they are regular fish balls with pork inside), fish tofu, save room for condensed milk drizzled fried mantou (fluffy buns). A solid joint for all you can eat hot pot that won't necessarily break the bank. The quality is a self-ascribed "solid" and is a great introduction to hotpot. Everything is ordered via QR code and on your phone so everyone at the table can order things incrementally. Service was fast. Was able to get a reservation easily.

DO NOT order the boba (the tapioca pearls were hard and the brown sugar one in particular was just lackluster). 

RANKING: GOOD
(terrible / bad / ok / GOOD/ great / excellent)
Absolutely love this spot for hot pot! They are so fast at getting additional veggies or meat for the unlimited hotpot. I love sitting at the upstairs tables its fun to see the entire place.

food was really delicious! my friend and i got sat quickly on a busy sunday night. the restaurant wasn't overly loud. i feel like the cost justified the meal--i left sooo full. 

one critique is to work on the vegetarian/non-pork soup bases! the veggie soup base was pretty bland when it arrived  but my friend was able to spice it up and make it tasty after adding seasonings and sauces from the bar.

but other than that, a great experience all around!
Prices amazing, Food Amazing. Super fun! Affordable, Reasonably priced hotpot and kbbq

We are extremely grateful to the staff that took us as a walk-in really late at night. We don't know if they were just being nice or if we were within their walk-in period, but regardless we are grateful. We really enjoyed everything we ate here. The cheese corn had a garlicky taste to it that went so well with all of the food. To be completely transparent, the sauce station was a bit messy, but I bring this up just to inform you about the atmosphere AT THAT TIME. It is important to remember that we did get here very late so that area was just simply the aftermath of a successful day of business. Regardless, if you are looking for an ayce bbq place or just end up in the area, check them out.

One of the must-see restaurants at night with delicious food, lovely staff, many ingredients to choose from, fresh and delicious food.

The staff is always on the look after and help. Unfortunately, this place is very dirty. Even though there are always customers

We got the hot pot- three flavors and tray after tray of meat, noodles, and veggies. The ambiance was amazing so we rate highly even though we had no idea what we were doing (we didn't know you cook your own food here!)
amazing service workers are all out going and make you feel comfortable and just an overall amazing experience and when it comes to the food, the food is amazing !!

I ate at 99 Favor Taste in the Chinatown two times. For both of them, I was sick after eating - abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, fatigue, brain frog, etc. 

I think the food they served was not fresh and/or had poor quality, maybe the leftovers for several days.

Also, the waitresses and waiters were not friendly at all. They were rude and inpatient. They hoped me to finish eating and leave as soon as possible because some customers were waiting for seats.

One more thing, the Free meal on Birthday is NOT real Free. They charge for tax, i.e. customers need to pay tax. Also they bluntly asked me for paying tips.

Really enjoyed my experience here! Been to both Brooklyn and Manhattan locations and it's always a good time due to the price for AYCE. Basically, you mix your own sauces at their station and then keep ordering meats that they cook in front of you. FYI: heavyyy pour for wine and it's just a yummy time. Def love this for a gathering with friends. Also, they took credit card so that was a happy surprise.

I enjoyed all their selections except for the vegetables which were not clean and I found a dead bug on it too, feel like they'll need to wash their veggies before serving to us customers. They have good amount of choices and overall a peaceful experience ( I stayed for 3 hours) it was $32.65 for one person after tax!
My favorite Hopot in New York, The service is cool, and nice decoration, it's a fun places to eat here. I love the environment. I would Love to come back. Food is stasty.

Just ok if you are within the area and every other restaurant is closed.

Staff weren't clear on who should be cooking, the guest or them. Also they seemed unclear as to who was eating from the grill (bbq) and who was eating soup (hot pot). Since I was the only one eating from the grill I didn't need all my items cooked at once. I was pacing myself, when on one of their walk bys they saw me cooking and decided to take it upon themselves to toss all my pork onto the grill and manhandle it. I said "I'm the only one eating bbq let's pace ourselves:)", they smiled and vanished. I took the pork's off when they were perfectly cooked. Right when I was about to grab one from the communal plate I set up (in case anyone wanted to try some) they returned and said "oh those aren't done". I said sure they are look, and cut one. "They chuckled and said "oh I can tell by looking, more time". While we were speaking they tossed them all back on the grill. Stood watch, cut all of them into unwanted super tiny pieces, and found one section of one piece slightly pink (fyi you can eat pink, not red). So now we had horribly overcooked rubber pork belly and only one guest at our table tried to eat it (they ate three pieces and called it quits. I tried one and after chewing for what felt like almost 20 minutes I was done). I proceeded to cook myself. At this point I felt as though I had to sneakily cook which made the experience tense :( I got pretty defensive like a mama bear protecting her cubs when they tried to touch my next protein. Luckily after that fiasco I got too eat well made chicken and lamb (they did attack our lamb and over cooked several of them but I managed to save 3 pieces). All drinks (tea, juice and alcoholic bevs) were disgusting and watery. A couple of items were missing, when asked about it and requested (several times) again they still never came. Oil for cooking was brought out at the tail end of the cooking experience. Music was horrible (unless you like pop mashups). Establishment was freezing. There aren't any vents so it got smokey fast (made me cough a few times). Walls are covered in grimey dust balls.

Overall if this is a hot pot joint that staff is to cook the food for the patrons then that should be made explicitly clear AND they must actually know how to cook. Seeing as this was not one of those spots it was highly uncomfortable. One and only positive note, their broths are pretty darn tasty (stars for the broth only.

I really had a negative experience at this location a few months ago. We were there for my friend's birthday. She had made a reservation for 6. We needed more room, I let the girl at the front who was doing seating know we were there for a reservation and needed to add two seats and she said OK. It was a bit loud so I double checked and asked if it was possible and she said Ok Ok No problem. I also let her know we needed a table, or half booth, because  some of the people in our party would have a difficult time in a booth. At this time I also asked for permission to bring our own 2 Liter Soda botte. The Brooklyn location allowed us to bring our own soda when I had my birthday there and I wanted to double check, the same girl said it was ok. 

When they sat us, they led us to....a 6 person booth in an elevated area. We tried to ask what was going on and explain, but they insisted we sit there, we managed to squeeze in but we werent too comfortable at all. One of our group was running late, and the other decided not to come when we let them know the table situation, but putting us into that situation was not professional. It became pretty obvious the girl at the front desk wasn't actually listening to what I said. When we asked for cups and opened our soda a manager came over to tell us not to, I explained we were given permission and the other issues with seating, he offered to move us, but at this point we were settled and had already ordered the first round of food, and it was pretty clear if he was going to move us to a larger table we'd have to go back up front to wait for them to clean it. 

Finally, the food itself was alright, it wasn't really out of this world quality it was just normal acceptable food. Delicious. However ordering the food was a nightmare, their bar code system was confusing.

I also gotta say, there was clearly some racial tension in the air as I caught them giving my partner dirty looks and I saw an item they were serving other customers but claimed they didn't have. It was pretty obvious.

I love KBBQ and Hot Pot but I cannot in good taste recommend this location. The Brooklyn location is much better as far as customer service goes.

I just walked in by myself, waitress took 12 minutes to talk to me (she was right at the entrance at the bar). Then pointed me to a table near the kitchen, no one was sitting there (seemwd loke an extra area for busy times, which is wasn't, it's 3pm). I asked if I could seat somewhere else, she said no, I left and she said too bad... well too bad, 1 less client and a lovely review!
The food was great! Ordering was seemless via the QR code. The macaroons... DELICIOUSSS!
Good service! I enjoyed the effort the workers put in serving our food! Thank you so much!

I'm disappointed that all the great reviews on Yelp let me down. 

This place definitely gets busy and you'll have to wait. But it's easy to track where you are in line through their system. 

Was seated for hot pot and of course out of ALL the seats and options in the restaurant we get a side table that wobbles, a portable gas stove and not real seats (fold up chairs). If I'm playing the same price as everyone else I should be able to sit at a regular table and be able to get the same experience. 

First of all you don't even get a waiter or waitress. No one tells you how it works or tells you where the sauce bar is. Had to figure it out on our own and wave down anyone we saw if we needed anything. The food came before our soup came and they was nothing we could do because we can't cook the food without soup. Asked the worker after 10 minutes of our food getting there if the soup is coming out yet, and I was given attitude. 

The sauce bar is so messy and everything is sticky. Also the floor is so slippery so be careful! Wish the sauce bar had ponzu sauce. 

The meat selection was decent. The meats itself weren't bad they were just avg. I had better meats at other hot pot places. The org broth is bland and the kimchi broth was not too spicy. 

They give out HUGE portions! So beware when ordering. If you're running low on soup no one will help you, you have to try to find a random worker. 

They do take card because I paid with card.

The restaurant as a whole just kind of feels dirty to me. Doesn't feel clean and the hostess was nonstop coughing and didn't cover her mouth once. Literally coughed by our table with out covering 10+ times. 

I'm highly dissatisfied with the service, the food, and the restaurant as a whole for the amount of good reviews this place has. 

I only had the hot pot, but I won't be back to try the bbq.

This is my go-to hot pot place. For AYCE in New York City, this restaurant is incredibly affordable. The menu includes beef and pork options (they recently added in pork belly, much to my delight), seafood, veggies, noodles, and among other items. With their selection of sauces, you have enough to make yourself a nice little signature concoction. 

I also appreciate the option to have individual pots (I like having my own, thank you!), which makes it easy for non-vegetarians and vegetarian friends to dine together.

The only aspect that could be improved here is the service. Mind you, this place gets VERY busy, which makes orders slow. Sometimes, orders won't come through their online ordering system, so you would have to re-order your items or ask the server for them again and again. But this one area of improvement isn't enough for me to quit this place. It's a go-to!

Cheap all you can eat hotpot place! When you are hungry, this is the best place to come. Soup bases are all delicious, I like yuan yang, mixing with spicy soup and the bone soup! Highly recommended :)
the food was delicious all the staff were super nice and friendly and the service was immaculate solid 10/10

I loved this place! It was all you can eat and I paid $37 total. The food was pretty good quality, lamb especially were super soft and tender. The bottom section was kind of a bbq place where you cook your own. They also had a self-serve sauce bar were you make your own sauce on the bottom floor where it comes with complementary milk, buns, and condensed milk. I also saw jelly, but they ran out when I was there.

I really liked my section on the second floor because the room was really spacious (I came with a group of 11 lol) one thing is that you can order online and they bring you your food based on the order however, they are really slow with that and we ended up not getting some of the food we ordered. So you have to ask the waiter repeatedly for your food.

But honestly for the price, this place is a must try! Can beat it anywhere else. Oh an they give you 8% off if you pay with cash.

got hotpot and it was super worth the price! i ate a ton of lamb (best meat fs) and fish fillet. we got individual pots but you can also choose to share a big pot! they also give an 8% discount with cash and have an atm right outside

At 29.99 for AYCE Hotpot in NY, overall it is pretty worth it if you're hungry. However, they were out of stock of the one of the more meats, including the Angus beef. Inside, the restaurant is well air-conditioned, and the staff was busy on a Tuesday night. The interior is quite well designed and minimal. Depending on the table that you get, you can do multiple individual pots. Overall pretty standard and nothing really stood out to me but it's a good place to go if you're hungry for hot pot.
Can't beat a free birthday meal! Huge variety of sauces. Hot Pot broth was delicious. Gyoza appetizer very good also. Skip the KBBQ, I thought the Hot Pot was better.

Food: 5/5 | Service: 5/5 | Experience: 4.5/5

This AYCE hot pot establishment is wonderful. They also have a KBBQ choice. The restaurant itself has the ability to host larger parties, and if it's your birthday, you get to eat free.

Each person gets their own hot pot to cook food in. The choices for meats are varied and good quality (there's beef, pork, lamb, etc). Everything that I would normally try to get at hot pot was there: pumpkin, taro, lotus root, fish roe, spinach, etc. The sauce station also boasted quite a bit of choice.

Service was really quick, and we ordered several times over the AYCE allotted period. At the end for my party of 7, we paid less than $40 to be stuffed with meat, vegetables, noodles, and complimentary yakult at the end.

My daughters took me here for my first time with BBQ. I have to say the food was awesome as my oldest was very enthusiastic about cooking the meats and veggies. The staff is friendly and intermittently check on your table. I'll be back for more. I had a great time.
got stomach flu from hotpot and gave it to my entire family. i've been here three times and will never come again.
Absolutely bussin cuh! Free ice cream was straight gas. Squid  hit different and the shrooms were tender and juicy.
Great food for an affordable price. About 27$ for ayce hotpot. Good quality ingredients! Will be back soon.

1. The food was delicious. We did the AYCE hot pot with spicy, traditional, and bone broth soup bases. I made my usual sauce mixture of sesame oil, chili oil, and chili paste. They had kimchi too, which was really good. 
2. The service was 9/10.
3. The place was dirty. The self-serve sauce bowls had clearly not been washed well - multiple bowls were covered in food from the previous users. The case was the same for the bowls provided at the tables. There were some teenagers taking pictures of themselves and vaping right over the side dishes and sauces for smoke in the pictures - none of the workers said anything. The side dishes were sitting open on a low counter, very easy for anyone's hairs to fall right in. 
4. It's LOUD. Korean BBQ + Shabu are social foods, but it was very difficult to hear what anyone was saying.

AYCE, order yourself on the phone hotpot for $30.. amaze deal!!

Standard hot pot and sauce options. Even had kimchi, sweet buns, fries, and fruit for free next to the sauce bar and free lil sweet candy and treats on the way out. Oh and a free yogurt digestive drink to cap it all off, great lil way to end the meal.

Can get busy, but can put ur name on waitlist and track it via website. Also lots of tables so waitlist moves quick.

Quick and easily located right off the Q line, 99 Favor is a great spot for BBQ/ Hotpot. Along with that, it's a great price for AYCE. You can chose between BBQ or Hotpot or both for a reasonable price. The quality of the food is good and flavorful. Quick and easy to order right off the QR code menu. It's a rather big place too - so it's easy to get a spot right off the bat. I definitely will be coming back. Totally worth it!
The food here is delicious and it's super clean. Love the waitresses as they are always there when we need help. Defined recommend !!!

(Overall: 95% | A) - 99 Favor Taste is a very unique restaurant in which you get free Hot Pot or KBBQ on your birthday if you bring a few friends along. The price is incredibly reasonable for AYCE hot pot in general, with an expansive menu and a large bar to make your own dipping sauce. Given the popularity, the service was a bit slow. The atmosphere is a bit cramped and if you are not here to troll your friends during their birthday, you might find the birthday song every 5 minutes a bit too much! Overall, I highly recommend taking someone here for their birthday -- it will be very memorable!

I just came here very recently; this past weekend and I really enjoyed my time at the restaurant. I've been to the location in Brooklyn and this one is much bigger. I like the ambience of the restaurant. It was really busy and loud but I could still hear my friend speak and enjoy a good conversation. The food was, very good, I got to try many different things since I came with a rather big group this time. We set a reservation and even though we got there a little late, we were showed right to our table with no huss or fuss which I appreciated because there is a lot of traffic in the city. I wasn't a big fan of the online menu, it was a little bit inconvenient for such a giant table because we had to pass one person's phone around. And some of the food came out rather late because of how busy it was in there and by the time a particular dish that I was looking forward to eating came out, I had already gotten full and only could eat one or two bites of it. So that was a little bit annoying but everything else was a really good experience.

Second time here, with a five-person group, even though we'd planned to eat elsewhere that night. 99 Favor had availability for hotpot after a 30-min wait, and we were just too hungry to consider anything else. I'll keep this review shot (my previous one is longer). The service is good, and the price for AYCE hotpot over here cannot be beaten! As for the food itself, it's standard hotpot food, without being overly fantastic, but certainly hitting the right spot. The sauce making station over here is one the big plusses!

a bit out of the way from the train stations in terms of common area but worth the trip and worth the effort to go to. One of the main features for me is the the face that you have a sauce bar with bowls ready to take back to your seat and a good amount of kimchi ready to just get from the bar as well. 

The options available to you from a hot pot perspective deff all you to keep the belly fed at least from a meat lovers perspective. then with the vegetables and roots there are sufficient options to choose from as well. 

There is an app that makes all of this simple and quick which streamlines the whole process. Be sure to get the pineapple and lettuce/romaine to cleanse the palette and to enable more eating. 

The quality of the meats were decent and were not too heavy on the fat but just enough to add flavor and not make it a issue. 

This will be a staple for me considering the location and options.

99 Favor is an ok place. Definitely worth a try but my party will likely not be going again.  They lured me in with the free birthday.  Who doesn't want to eat free on their birthday.  However the greeting was quick and we're seated immediately for our reservation. FYI, The place was packed. The customer service was poor. I felt like I was at a Karen restaurant where they don't yell at you. I can't emphasize on how many plates and bowls were practically slammed on the table.  
The food came out fast as well as the  drinks.  The prices were decent definitely budget friendly.  The sauce section was limited and weren't told about it until we asked where it was. 

The food was ok, I've had better quality at other hot pot and  bbq places. 

The table were spacious  and decor  didn't catch my eye.   

You pay for the service you receive.

The second we walked in, we were drawn by the wafting aromas of meat, fried vegetal protein, and deep rich broth. We had just returned to New York from the Dominican Republic and were craving hot pot while in customs, so we Ubered straight to here with our luggage. 

99 Favor Taste is an iconic hot-pot staple in New York. 

This place is cavernous compared to your traditional mom-and-pop hot-pot restaurants in New York City. Spacious and comfortable, modern yet a bit gimmicky with the intermittent birthday mascot, it doesn't take away any points for this popular joint. 

It's also a plus that you can order hot pot and BBQ.

Service was quick, not all that personable, but sufficient for a hot pot restaurant. 

The fried tofu skin, winter melon, caviar fish cake pockets, and squid are topping my list. We also had requisite lamb, beef, fuzhou and fish balls, fish cake, shrooms, vermicelli, tripe, etc. We opted for half spicy and half pork bone broth.

All in all, this is the best budget hot-pot that doesn't feel budget-y, but there are a few cons, as mentioned by other Yelpers:

1. The "clean" plates were not clean. I understand this restaurant's profit margins are thin, and they rely heavily on getting people in and out, but, unfortunately, sanitation was an issue here. Be wary of the "clean" plates they have set up by the sauce bar. 

2. Some broth options (especially the pork bone) could be better. Avoid pork bone broth at all costs. As others mentioned, it's just water with a few peppers. Different from what we were expecting. 

3. As others mentioned, don't expect high-quality meat here. Not a single bit. You'll get semi-frozen, bottom-shelf slices of beef. Vegetables? Honestly, not the freshest. But I can't ding them for that, given the price point. For under $30 per person for AYCE, this is, by far, the best you can get in New York City. 

We landed in JFK quite late at night and only had a few hot-pot options, so we went with 99 Favor Taste. Will we come back? Likely not. Was it still worth it? Absolutely!
Amazing food selections and services. Never seems to fail and the fact that a person eat for free on the birthday is amazing.

Terrible service. Our waitress with the short wavy hair and glasses looked like she did not enjoy her job. She did not communicate to us whatsoever and never came to check up on us or even drop off our check. Whenever she did come to our table we felt as if we were not welcomed.

Absolutely horrible. Disgusting level of cleanliness and meat quality. As much as they missed the "L" in "Flavor", this restaurant makes up for it by being a huge L.

I'd like to begin with saying I live in Southern California where we're somewhat spoiled by all of the AYCE hotpots and/or BBQs (Korean especially) down here simply due to competition and concentration. I'm confident in saying I have plenty of experience with all three kinds (AYCE BBQ, AYCE Hotpot, and AYCE hybrid BBQ + Hotpot) of establishments from my 10+ years here.

I'd also begin with personal experience of no restaurant I've been to that serves both hotpot & bbq is ever good at both.

--

We went here for a friend's birthday (and the meal was free for birthday person), and the part in parenthesis should've been enough of a sign to stay away.

Hotpot:
The broths were ok, ordered the Kimchi broth and it was decent but tasted like salted water with a hint of savory. Tried the Tonkotsu and Mala pots as well, and both were the same. Pot controls were in Chinese, which I could see as being confusing to non-Chinese speakers.

BBQ:
Crappy grill with barely any space to cook anything, not oiled at all like other BBQ places do. The worst part though was that during grill changes, the employees simply just grabbed the grill, with NO TRAY under it, and walked it on the main floors to the back... Dripping grease and food remnants ALL OVER the main walkways. No wonder we saw two people slip during our short hour and a half there.

Meat quality:
The Hotpot "beef" was the ONLY good meat they had, and it was a crappy cut of USDA Select level beef. Picture attached. We ended up using it for the bbq as well since it was the only meat that seemed like real meat.

The rest of the meat? Defrosted. Smelled AND tasted expired. Turned into a pale gray when cooked. Even the assortment of marinades they had, including the house special, could not mask the flavor/smell of spoiled beef.

This included the chicken and pork as well - slimy, smelly, and gross.

Sure it's not a premium AYCE, but the meats had no marbling, were chewy, no texture, and just plain gross.

Cleanliness:
Almost EVERY bowl and spoon we encountered, both at the self-serve sauce & appetizer area as well as table service were DIRTY, NOT FULLY CLEAN, and had either dirt and/or dried food from the previous user on it. We had to literally ask multiple times for clean dishes until they finally gave us a freshly washed (rinsed?) one.

Staff:
Everyone who worked there seemed like they absolutely hated their job. We inquired about the tastes of the broth and asked for recommendations to fit our pro-spicy tastes, and two employees just gave us attitude and said order whatever we want.

Will NEVER come back and advised all of my friends that live in/plan to visit NYC to avoid this place like the plague. You might catch it by eating here - all 4 of us had stomachaches for the next day or two, and I'm thinking it was because of the health hazard this joke of a restaurant is.

I always come to this place when I visit NY - you can do either kbbq or hot pot or both. It's a cheap option for AYCE and provides a variety of choices. They have a lot of seating but due to popularity, it still takes a while to get seated on a busy day. The meat quality is pretty bad Ngl but what can you expect out of an all you can eat? 

The staff weren't exactly friendly, but were efficient in the way they work and they brought out our food pretty fast. 

They have a good choice of sauces at their sauce station for you to make what you like. 

It gets a little annoying when they play the birthday song every 2 minutes but hey free ice cream.

Swift serving Korean BBQ and Hotpot spot with all you can eat options that are very affordable for city prices. Everything is solid but definitely try the underrated imitation crab. $30 a person. 4/5 stars as a lunch spot.

Came here with some friends six months ago as we had some old classmates who'd just moved to the city. This was maybe my second or third time with hot pot, and while I love the flavors, I don't think I enjoy the activity itself. The staff were not helpful at all in explaining what's best to order, what we must try, how long to keep different things in the broth. Overall, a very disorganized experience if you're even semi-new to it. Maybe it's just the idea of grilling meats instead of boiling them in a spicy broth, but I much prefer something like Japanese or Korean BBQ if I'm gonna get a crowd together. Nothing is necessarily "wrong" with this place, I think it's just a "me problem".

Food was fine, the price was high, but I did leave full. This was so borderline, I can't decide if it gets a recommendation or not--I'm just that ambivalent. I guess if you're wanting hot pot specifically, then this is a fine place to go; but, if you're wanting to try something different from your usual thing, then this is maybe not the most accessible place. Good luck, though!

Food: I absolutely loved everything here. The meats were all fresh and tender, the sides were also really good. We got the AYCE BBQ & Hot Pot Set so we were able to enjoy both boiling and grilling our meats. The menu has a lot of variety which gave us an opportunity to taste everything. We also had variety with our individual hot pot broths so that we could try three different broths and everything was so good!

Ambiance: The ambiance is really chill and I love dim lighting in the place. It makes it feel a lot cozier which was exactly what I usually feel when having hot pot and/or barbecue. It definitely matched the food and made the overall vibe a lot better.
好评 吃的火锅都是来99，服务ok价格实惠。菜很多。朋友之前这里上班说待遇不错。 关键菜好吃。时间无限 特别适合朋友聚餐.今天健身完刚过来大餐一顿增肌很不错. 食品很丰富 朋友聚餐的好选择！

Nice place. Worth the waiting. This is my second time here. 很好吃的火锅加烧烤，自助式设计很不错，很满足 
曼岛还不错的自助 周末记得提前预约

一年半前和朋友来纽约旅游吃的，当时找火锅就找到这个。反正我吃的很爽，毕竟任吃，拍了一会队，最后狂吃了好久吃撑。味道都说得过去，对于难得吃到火锅的人已经很满足了。人有点多咯。
来过很多次了，从BK的老店到唐人街的新店我都是支持者哈哈，贴心的服务，工作人员的服务态度很专业很友好有耐心，食物也新鲜，我喜欢吃鱼，希望火锅鱼片不要放太多粉腌制，我会继续支持你们的，呵呵~

NY来てから、ずっと食べたかった物のひとつ、本格火鍋！こちらのお店は食べ放題なので、料金を気にしないでたくさん食べられます。
spicy hot potは現地の香辛料(四川風？)がふんだんに使われており、本当に本当に美味しかったです！辛いものが苦手な人はやめといた方が吉。
Chinese herbal hot pot(薬膳鍋)は、思っていたよりも食べやすく、病みつきになる味。どっちも本当におすすめします！
またビールがめちゃくちゃリーズナブル！小ビンビールが2.5〜3ドルと破格となっております。物価の高いマンハッタンでは、こんなに安いのは初めてでした。
ひとつだけ悔しかったのが、本場では各自でオリジナルのつけダレを作成するらしく、なかなかコツが掴めなかったこと。何種類もの薬味と調味料を調合しなければなりません。ぜひ、またチャレンジしたいです。
美味しさ+楽しさがあり、友人や家族を連れてワイワイやりたいお店です。
炒鸡赞 炒鸡好吃的店 推荐5服务很贴心 pretty nice place. Like hot pot &BBQ. COOL PLACE

Ce restaurant est exeptionel il est très dur de trouve a NY des restaurant a volonté  de cette qualité , la première chose magique est l odeurs qui a en dégage Mgr depuis l extérieur ( magique !!!) le personnel est très simpatique la nourriture de très bonne qualité pour un prix très correct , en weekend le restaurant est souvent complet et il faut compte 1h30 d attente alors si vous pouvez réservez ou aller tard le soir ! 

This restaurant is amaizing ! Good food good service amaizing ambiance !! Often crowded ( 1h30 waiting during weekend ) i advise you to go during the week or late in the weekend , the food have a really good value as it is a All you can eat, the barbecue table are really fun for a friend dinner !
